sections.title: Economics of Having It All
sections.description:
This class will cover the economics of crafting a life that works for you, navigating life’s differences and difficulties, guided by economic theory and empirical evidence. We will cover everything from defining your own unique utility function to when to lean in at work and when to level up, to fertility timing and dividing domestic work with your partner, to discrimination and external constraints, to what to outsource.
The format will be discussion based, with a short lecture each session and then active class discussion, and small group exercises drawing parallels between economic research and students’ own lives. Note that although many of the readings are research papers, students are only expected to come to class having read only the introduction of the paper and skimming the rest, except for papers a student chooses to present. Readings are critical to an engaged class discussion, so we will have a short paper quiz at the beginning of each class.
You will work intensively with a small group throughout the class, and both group and class participation counts towards your final grade.
